chapters.title: Two ways and their outcomes

parts.text: The blessed person refuses the counsel and company of the wicked and delights instead in the LORD’s law, meditating on it day and night. Such a life resembles a well-watered, fruitful tree. The ungodly are compared to windblown chaff and cannot stand in the judgment or among the righteous. The LORD knows the righteous way, while the way of the ungodly ends in destruction.

chapters.title: The LORD establishes his anointed king

parts.text: Nations and rulers conspire against the LORD and his anointed, determined to throw off their authority. God laughs at their rebellion and declares that he has established his king on Zion. Human opposition cannot cancel his decree.

The king recounts the LORD’s declaration that he is his Son and will receive the nations as an inheritance, ruling them with decisive power. Kings and judges are therefore urged to act wisely, serve the LORD with fear, and kiss the Son. Those who trust in him are blessed; rebellion exposes them to wrath.

chapters.title: Confidence amid multiplying enemies

parts.text: Surrounded by enemies who say God will not help him, the psalmist calls the LORD his shield, glory, and the one who lifts his head. God answers from his holy hill, enabling him to lie down, sleep, and wake without fear despite the forces surrounding him. He asks the LORD to arise and break his enemies’ power, declaring that salvation belongs to the LORD and his blessing rests upon his people.

chapters.title: Peace that outlasts distress

parts.text: The psalmist appeals to the God who has relieved him before and rebukes those who love vanity and falsehood. The LORD hears the godly, so people should examine themselves, refrain from sin, offer righteous sacrifices, and trust him. God’s favour brings greater gladness than an abundant harvest. With that assurance, the psalmist can lie down peacefully, because his safety ultimately rests with the LORD.

chapters.title: A morning prayer for guidance

parts.text: The psalmist brings his prayer to the LORD in the morning and waits expectantly. God does not delight in wickedness, lies, violence, or deceit. By contrast, the worshipper enters God’s house through abundant mercy and bows toward the holy temple in reverence.

He asks to be led in righteousness and given a straight path because of watching enemies. Their flattering words conceal corruption, and he asks that their own counsels bring them down. The psalm closes by calling those who trust God to rejoice, since his favour surrounds the righteous like a shield.

chapters.title: Tears give way to confidence

parts.text: Weak and deeply troubled, the psalmist asks the LORD not to rebuke him in anger but to heal and deliver him in mercy. He wonders how long relief will be delayed, describing nights soaked with tears and eyes worn by grief. Then his tone changes: the LORD has heard his weeping and received his prayer. He tells workers of iniquity to depart and anticipates the shame and retreat of his enemies.

chapters.title: An appeal to the righteous judge

parts.text: The psalmist seeks refuge from pursuers and invites judgment upon himself if he has committed the wrong alleged against him. He asks the LORD to arise, judge the peoples, vindicate his integrity, end wickedness, and establish the just. God examines hearts and inward motives.

God is described as a righteous judge who prepares weapons against the unrepentant. The wicked conceive trouble, dig a pit, and fall into the destruction they intended for others. Their violence returns upon their own heads. The psalmist concludes by praising the righteousness and name of the LORD Most High.

chapters.title: Human dignity under the Creator

parts.text: The psalm praises the LORD’s excellent name and glory above the heavens. God ordains strength out of the mouth of babes and sucklings to still the enemy and the avenger. Looking at the moon and stars, the psalmist wonders why God cares for humanity, yet recognizes the honour God has given people: crowned with glory and entrusted with dominion over the animals, birds, and sea creatures. The wonder at human responsibility returns to praise of the LORD’s majesty throughout the earth.

chapters.title: God remembers the oppressed

parts.text: The psalmist thanks the LORD wholeheartedly for judging his cause and defeating hostile nations. Their cities and memory perish, but God’s throne endures. He judges the world righteously and serves as a refuge for the oppressed; those who know his name trust him because he does not abandon those who seek him.

The people are called to proclaim God’s works in Zion. The psalmist asks for deliverance so he can continue praising, describes nations caught in their own snares, and affirms that the needy will not always be forgotten. He asks God to arise and teach the nations their human limits.

chapters.title: Why does the wicked oppressor seem secure?

parts.text: The psalm begins by asking why the LORD seems distant in trouble. It describes an arrogant oppressor who boasts of desire, dismisses God, and assumes lasting security. With lies, threats, and concealed violence, he hunts the helpless and imagines that God neither notices nor remembers.

The psalmist asks God to arise and remember the afflicted. God has seen the harm and grief, and the helpless entrust themselves to him. The prayer seeks the breaking of wicked power and a full accounting of wrongdoing. The LORD’s enduring kingship gives assurance that he hears the humble and will defend the fatherless and oppressed.

chapters.title: Trust when foundations seem destroyed

parts.text: The psalmist refuses advice to flee like a bird, even when the wicked secretly aim at the upright and society’s foundations appear ruined. The LORD remains in his holy temple, with his throne in heaven, observing and testing humanity. He examines the righteous but hates violence and will judge the wicked. His own righteousness is the basis of his love for righteous conduct and his regard for the upright.

chapters.title: Pure words amid flattering speech

parts.text: The psalmist asks for help as faithful people disappear and flattering, double-hearted speech prevails. Those who boast that their tongues make them independent will be cut off. The LORD declares that he will arise for the oppressed poor and needy. Unlike deceitful human words, his words are pure as thoroughly refined silver. The psalm closes with confidence in his preservation even while corrupt people gain honour around them.

chapters.title: How long will sorrow continue?

parts.text: The psalmist repeatedly asks how long God will seem to forget him, hide his face, and leave him grieving while an enemy triumphs. He begs for an answer and renewed strength before death or defeat gives his opponents reason to rejoice. Yet the prayer ends in trust: he relies on God’s mercy, anticipates joy in salvation, and resolves to sing because the LORD has dealt generously with him.

chapters.title: Corruption and the hope of Israel’s salvation

parts.text: The fool denies God in his heart, and the psalm describes widespread corruption: the LORD looks for understanding and goodness but finds humanity turned aside. Evildoers consume God’s people as casually as bread and do not call upon him. Nevertheless, God is among the righteous and is the poor person’s refuge. The final prayer longs for salvation from Zion and the restoration that will make Jacob and Israel rejoice.

chapters.title: Who may dwell with the LORD?

parts.text: The psalm asks who may dwell in the LORD’s tabernacle and holy hill. The answer describes a life of integrity: truthful speech, refusal to slander or harm a neighbour, honour for those who fear God, and faithfulness to an oath even at personal cost. Such a person will not exploit others through lending or accept bribes against the innocent. This steady righteousness is associated with a life that will not be moved.

chapters.title: The LORD is the chosen inheritance

parts.text: The psalmist seeks preservation in God and delights in the faithful rather than joining the worship of other gods. Those who pursue another god multiply their sorrows. The LORD himself is the psalmist’s portion and the one who maintains his inheritance.

He celebrates a good inheritance and the LORD’s counsel, setting God always before him. This confidence brings joy and hope even in the face of death: God will not abandon his soul in hell or allow his Holy One to see corruption. God’s presence reveals life’s path, fullness of joy, and enduring pleasures.

chapters.title: Protection beneath God’s wings

parts.text: The psalmist asks God to hear a sincere plea and examine his conduct. He maintains that he has avoided the destroyer’s paths and asks that his steps be kept steady. His appeal rests on God’s wondrous lovingkindness toward those who seek refuge from adversaries.

He asks to be guarded like the apple of an eye and hidden beneath God’s wings from enemies who surround him like a stalking lion. He requests deliverance from people whose portion is in this life and whose prosperity passes to their children. His own hope is to behold God’s face in righteousness and be satisfied with his likeness.

chapters.title: A song of rescue and victorious strength

parts.text: The psalmist praises the LORD as rock, fortress, shield, and deliverer. Surrounded by the cords of death, he cried out and was heard. God’s intervention is pictured through earthquake, fire, storm, and waters as he rescues his servant from powerful enemies. The psalmist connects this deliverance with his faithfulness to God’s ways.

God deals faithfully with the faithful, humbles the proud, and gives light and strength. He equips the psalmist for battle, enables him to overcome enemies, and establishes authority among nations. Praise rises to the living God who grants victories and shows lasting mercy to his anointed, David, and his descendants.

chapters.title: Creation’s witness and the LORD’s instruction

parts.text: The heavens proclaim God’s glory day after day and night after night. Their witness reaches throughout the world, and the sun is pictured as a bridegroom and a strong runner crossing the heavens. Nothing escapes its heat.

The LORD’s law, testimony, statutes, and commandments restore, enlighten, and guide. They are more desirable than gold and sweeter than honey, warning God’s servant and bringing reward in obedience. Recognizing hidden faults as well as deliberate sins, the psalmist asks to be cleansed and kept from presumptuous wrongdoing. He wants both his speech and inward meditation to be acceptable to his redeemer.

chapters.title: Confidence before battle

parts.text: The people pray that the LORD will answer their king in trouble, defend him, remember his offerings, and grant his purposes. They anticipate rejoicing in God’s salvation and raising banners in his name. Confidence rests in the LORD’s ability to save his anointed from heaven. Others depend on chariots and horses, but God’s people remember his name. The psalm closes with a plea for salvation and an answer when they call.

chapters.title: Thanksgiving for the king’s victory

parts.text: The king rejoices in the LORD’s strength and salvation. God has answered his desire, welcomed him with blessings, given him a crown, and granted life, honour, and gladness. His stability rests on trust in the LORD and the mercy of the Most High.

The psalm then anticipates judgment upon the king’s enemies. Their hostile schemes will fail, their strength and descendants will be cut off, and divine wrath will overtake them. The closing prayer asks the LORD to be exalted in his own strength, while the worshippers promise to celebrate his power with song.

chapters.title: Abandonment gives way to worldwide praise

parts.text: The speaker cries out to God in apparent abandonment, recalling how earlier generations trusted and were delivered. Mockers challenge his reliance on the LORD. Surrounded by enemies pictured as bulls, lions, and dogs, he describes bodily agony, pierced hands and feet, and garments divided by lot. He pleads urgently for rescue.

The tone turns to testimony and praise among the congregation because God has heard the afflicted person’s cry. The poor are satisfied, and the ends of the world turn to worship the LORD, whose kingdom embraces the nations. Future generations will hear of his righteousness and declare what he has done.

chapters.title: The LORD as shepherd and host

parts.text: The psalmist describes the LORD as his shepherd, providing rest, refreshment, restoration, and guidance in righteous paths. Even in the valley of the shadow of death, God’s presence and care remove fear. The image becomes that of a generous host who prepares a table despite surrounding enemies and gives overflowing provision. Confident of continuing goodness and mercy, the psalmist looks forward to dwelling in the LORD’s house forever.

chapters.title: Welcoming the King of glory

parts.text: The earth and everyone in it belong to the LORD, who established the world upon the waters. Those who approach his holy place must have clean hands and pure hearts, refusing falsehood and deceit. Such people receive blessing and righteousness from the God of their salvation.

The gates are commanded to lift up so the King of glory may enter. The repeated question about his identity receives an emphatic answer: he is the LORD, strong and mighty in battle, the LORD of hosts. Ownership of the whole earth frames the call for holy approach and royal welcome.

chapters.title: A prayer for teaching, pardon, and rescue

parts.text: The psalmist entrusts himself to the LORD, asking not to be put to shame by enemies. He seeks instruction in God’s paths and asks God to remember mercy rather than the sins of his youth. Because the LORD is good and upright, he teaches sinners and guides the meek. His paths are mercy and truth to those who keep his covenant and testimonies, and the psalmist asks pardon for his great iniquity.

He describes the blessing of those who fear God: instruction, covenant understanding, and an enduring inheritance. Lonely, afflicted, and surrounded by enemies, he seeks forgiveness and deliverance. He asks that integrity preserve him and that God redeem Israel from all its troubles.

chapters.title: Integrity and love for God’s house

parts.text: The psalmist invites the LORD to examine his heart and conduct, affirming trust in God and a refusal to join deceitful or violent people. He loves God’s house and approaches the altar with thanksgiving, wanting to proclaim the LORD’s wonderful works. He asks not to be swept away with sinners whose hands hold wrongdoing and bribes. Relying on redemption and mercy, he anticipates standing securely and blessing the LORD among the congregation.

chapters.title: Seeking God’s face without fear

parts.text: The LORD is the psalmist’s light, salvation, and strength, so enemies and even an army cannot finally govern his confidence. His deepest request is to dwell in the LORD’s house, behold his beauty, and seek him there. God’s shelter will raise him above danger, prompting joyful offerings and song.

The prayer asks God to hear, receive, and teach him rather than abandon him to false witnesses. Even if father and mother forsake him, the LORD will receive him. Confidence in seeing God’s goodness sustains him, and the closing exhortation urges patient, courageous waiting upon the LORD.

chapters.title: A plea that becomes thanksgiving

parts.text: The psalmist cries to the LORD as his rock, fearing the silence that would leave him like those descending to the pit. He asks not to share the fate of people whose peaceful speech hides malicious hearts. Because they disregard God’s works, he asks that their own deeds receive their proper recompense.

He then blesses the LORD for hearing his plea. His heart trusts in God as strength and shield, and help brings joyful praise. The prayer widens from personal deliverance to the LORD’s people and anointed, asking that God save, bless, feed, and uphold his inheritance forever.

chapters.title: The LORD’s voice over the storm

parts.text: The mighty are called to give the LORD glory and worship in holiness. His voice thunders over the waters, breaks cedars, shakes the wilderness, and strips forests bare. The storm displays a majesty that prompts worshippers in his temple to cry glory. Yet the LORD’s power is not momentary: he sits as king over the flood and forever. The psalm ends with his gifts of strength and peace to his people.

chapters.title: Mourning turned into dancing

parts.text: The psalmist praises the LORD for rescue from death and for refusing his enemies the satisfaction of his defeat. He calls the faithful to give thanks, contrasting the brevity of God’s anger with the life found in his favour: a night of weeping gives way to morning joy.

He remembers assuming that his prosperity could never be shaken, then becoming troubled when God hid his face. He pleaded for mercy and preservation so he could continue praising. God changed mourning into dancing and removed sackcloth in favour of gladness. The psalmist therefore commits himself to enduring thanksgiving.

chapters.title: Trusting God through rejection and danger

parts.text: The psalmist seeks refuge in the LORD as a strong rock and commits his spirit into God’s hand. He rejoices in mercy but describes grief, failing strength, rejection by neighbours, and conspiracies against his life. Feeling forgotten like a dead man, he still appeals to the God who knows his adversity.

He declares that his times are in God’s hand and asks deliverance from enemies and false accusers. God’s goodness provides shelter for those who trust him. Remembering that God heard even when he thought himself cut off, he calls the faithful to love the LORD and urges all who hope in him to take courage.

chapters.title: The blessing of confessed and forgiven sin

parts.text: The psalm celebrates the happiness of the person whose sin is forgiven and no longer charged against him. Concealment brought wasting distress under God’s heavy hand. When the psalmist acknowledged his transgression instead of hiding it, the LORD forgave his guilt.

The godly are urged to pray while God may be found, trusting him as a hiding place amid trouble. Instruction follows, warning against the stubbornness of a horse or mule that must be restrained. Many sorrows belong to the wicked, but mercy surrounds the one who trusts the LORD. The righteous are called to rejoice.

chapters.title: The Creator watches over those who fear him

parts.text: The righteous are invited to praise with instruments and a new song. God’s word is right and his works faithful; he made the heavens by his word and gathers the waters under his command. All the earth should stand in awe. Nations’ counsels fail, but the LORD’s counsel stands through every generation.

God looks down upon all people, understanding their hearts and works. Neither armies, personal strength, nor horses guarantee deliverance. His eye rests upon those who fear him and hope in his mercy, preserving them even amid death and famine. The worshippers wait upon him as their help and shield, asking mercy in accordance with their hope.

chapters.title: Taste and see the LORD’s goodness

parts.text: The psalmist promises continual praise and invites the humble to join him in magnifying the LORD. He sought God and was delivered from fear; the poor person’s cry was heard. The LORD’s angel surrounds those who fear him, and those who seek him lack no good thing. The invitation is to taste and see his goodness.

Instruction in fearing the LORD follows: guard speech, leave evil, do good, seek peace, and pursue it. God hears the righteous and draws near to the brokenhearted. Their afflictions may be many, but he delivers them and preserves his servants, while evil destroys the wicked.

chapters.title: A plea against malicious and ungrateful enemies

parts.text: The psalmist asks the LORD to fight those who fight him and turn their hidden snares against them. He promises praise for the rescue of the powerless from stronger oppressors. False witnesses rise against him, and people for whom he once fasted and grieved now gather to celebrate his stumbling.

He asks how long God will look on without rescuing him. Enemies who hate him without cause must not triumph through false accusations or dishonest claims of success. He appeals for righteous judgment and looks forward to public thanksgiving. Those who favour his just cause should rejoice and magnify the LORD, who delights in his servant’s well-being.

chapters.title: Wickedness contrasted with abundant mercy

parts.text: The wicked person’s conduct reveals a lack of fear before God. Self-flattery conceals the seriousness of wrongdoing, deceit replaces wise speech, and evil plans are formed even in bed. The person settles on a harmful path without rejecting evil.

The LORD’s mercy, faithfulness, righteousness, and judgments are described through the vastness of heaven, mountains, and the deep. People find refuge beneath his wings and abundant provision in his house. He is the fountain of life and source of light. The prayer asks continued lovingkindness and protection from pride and violence, while anticipating the fall of evildoers.

chapters.title: Do not envy the wicked

parts.text: The psalm urges patience rather than anger or envy when evildoers prosper. Their success withers like grass, while those who trust the LORD, do good, and wait upon him receive an enduring inheritance. The meek inherit the earth. The little owned by the righteous is better than the wealth of many wicked, whose power will be broken.

Generosity, justice, and upright speech characterize the righteous, whom God upholds even when they stumble. Apparent wicked strength may disappear like a flourishing tree suddenly gone. The upright person’s end is peace, but transgressors are cut off together. Salvation, strength in trouble, and final deliverance come from the LORD to those who trust him.

chapters.title: Sickness, guilt, and a plea for mercy

parts.text: The psalmist asks the LORD not to rebuke him in wrath. He describes bodily pain and overwhelming guilt, acknowledging that his foolishness has brought grievous wounds and unrest. Friends stand apart from his suffering, while enemies lay traps and invent deceit. He remains like a deaf and silent man rather than answering them.

His hope is that the LORD will answer. Ready to fall, he confesses his iniquity and sorrow over sin, but also protests the strength of those who hate him wrongfully and oppose him for pursuing good. He begs God not to forsake him and asks his salvation to come quickly.

chapters.title: Teach me the measure of my days

parts.text: The psalmist tries to guard his tongue in the presence of the wicked, but suppressed sorrow grows until he speaks to God. He asks to understand life’s brevity. Human days are only a handbreadth, and the bustle of accumulating wealth leaves uncertainty about who will finally possess it.

His hope therefore rests in the Lord. He asks deliverance from transgressions and removal of the chastening that consumes his strength. Recognizing himself as a stranger and temporary resident before God, he pleads for his tears to be heard and for a little restored strength before his life ends.

chapters.title: Rescued to obey and proclaim

parts.text: The psalmist remembers waiting for the LORD, who lifted him from a pit, set his feet securely, and gave him a new song. God’s wonderful works exceed telling. Beyond sacrifice alone, the speaker delights in doing God’s will, keeps his law within, and publicly declares his righteousness, faithfulness, and salvation.

New troubles and countless iniquities now overwhelm him. He asks that enemies seeking his destruction be ashamed, while those who love God’s salvation rejoice and magnify him. Despite being poor and needy, he knows the Lord thinks of him. He urgently calls upon his help and deliverer not to delay.

chapters.title: Mercy in sickness and betrayal

parts.text: The psalm begins with blessing upon those who consider the poor and confidence that the LORD sustains them in trouble and sickness. The speaker asks mercy and healing, admitting sin, while enemies speculate about his death and spread malicious reports. Even a trusted companion who shared his bread has turned against him. He asks God to raise him up and preserve his integrity. The psalm closes by blessing the LORD God of Israel forever.

chapters.title: Thirsting for God in a time of sorrow

parts.text: The psalmist longs for God as a deer longs for water. Tears and the repeated taunt asking where his God is sharpen his grief. He remembers joining joyful crowds in worship and questions his own despair, urging his soul to hope in God because praise will yet return.

Distance, overwhelming waters, and persistent enemies describe the continuing distress. Still, he remembers the LORD’s daytime lovingkindness and the prayer and song of the night. He asks why he seems forgotten, then repeats the call to hope in God, who remains his salvation and his God.

chapters.title: Light and truth lead back to worship

parts.text: The psalmist asks God to defend his cause against deceitful and unjust people. Though God is his strength, he feels rejected and mourns beneath enemy oppression. He asks for God’s light and truth to lead him to the holy hill and dwelling place, where he will approach the altar with joyful praise. The closing words again confront his downcast soul and urge hope in God, whom he expects to praise.

chapters.title: A defeated people appeals to covenant mercy

parts.text: The people remember hearing how God drove out nations and planted their ancestors in the land. Victory came through his favour, not their swords or strength. They call him their king and trust him to defeat their enemies, resolving to praise his name.

Yet their present experience is defeat, scattering, plunder, and public shame. They insist they have not forgotten God’s covenant or turned to other gods, although they are treated as sheep for slaughter. The prayer asks why God seems asleep and hides his face. It ends with a plea that he arise, help, and redeem them for his mercy’s sake.

chapters.title: A royal wedding song

parts.text: The singer praises the king’s gracious speech, majesty, and victory in the cause of truth, meekness, and righteousness. His throne and righteous sceptre endure, and his love of righteousness is honoured with joyful anointing. Rich garments, ivory palaces, and royal attendants surround him.

The bride is urged to leave her former people and household and honour the king. She is brought in splendid clothing with rejoicing companions, while wealthy visitors seek her favour. The song anticipates sons becoming princes and promises that the king’s name will be remembered through generations, bringing enduring praise.

chapters.title: God is refuge amid upheaval

parts.text: Because God is refuge and strength, his people need not fear even if the earth shakes and mountains fall into the sea. A river gladdens God’s city, where his presence secures it despite raging nations and tottering kingdoms. The LORD of hosts is with his people. His works bring desolation to hostile power and end wars. The command to be still and acknowledge God accompanies his promise to be exalted among the nations and throughout the earth.

chapters.title: Praise the King of all the earth

parts.text: All peoples are called to clap and shout in triumph because the LORD Most High is the great king over the earth. He subdues nations and chooses the inheritance of the people he loves. God ascends amid shouts and trumpet sound, prompting repeated calls to sing praise with understanding. He reigns over the nations from his holy throne, and the rulers of the peoples gather before the God of Abraham, to whom earthly power belongs.

chapters.title: Zion displays the LORD’s protection

parts.text: The LORD is praised in his holy city, Mount Zion, the joy of the whole earth. God is known as a refuge within her palaces. Assembled kings see the city and flee in panic, like sailors whose ships are shattered by an east wind. What the worshippers heard about God’s protection they have now seen.

They meditate on God’s lovingkindness in the temple and praise his righteousness throughout the earth. Zion rejoices in his judgments. The people are urged to examine the city’s towers and defences so they can tell the next generation that this God will remain their God and guide even to death.

chapters.title: Wealth cannot ransom a life

parts.text: The psalm addresses rich and poor alike with wisdom about wealth and mortality. There is no reason to fear those who trust in riches, for no person can buy another’s release from death or secure endless earthly life. Wise and foolish alike die, leaving possessions behind despite naming lands after themselves.

Those who trust their own prosperity are led toward the grave, where their beauty and power disappear. The psalmist instead trusts God to redeem his soul from the power of the grave. A rich person’s honour does not accompany him at death. Honour without understanding leaves a person like the beasts that perish.

chapters.title: God calls his worshippers to account

parts.text: The mighty God summons the earth and gathers his covenant people for judgment. He does not rebuke them for a shortage of sacrifices: every animal already belongs to him, and he needs no food from human hands. He calls instead for thanksgiving, fulfilled vows, and prayer in trouble, promising deliverance that will glorify him.

God then challenges people who recite his statutes while hating instruction, supporting theft and adultery, and spreading slander. His previous silence must not be mistaken for approval. They must reconsider before judgment comes. Genuine praise and rightly ordered conduct honour God and accompany the revelation of his salvation.

chapters.title: A plea for cleansing and a renewed heart

parts.text: The psalmist appeals to God’s abundant mercy to blot out transgression and wash away sin. He acknowledges wrongdoing openly, recognizing God’s justice and his own deeply rooted uncleanness. God desires truth within, so the plea seeks inward wisdom, purification, restored joy, and the removal of guilt from God’s sight.

He asks for a clean heart, a renewed spirit, continuing fellowship, and restored joy in salvation. Then he will teach sinners and praise God for deliverance from bloodguilt. A broken and contrite heart matters beyond sacrifice alone. The closing prayer asks good for Zion and the rebuilding of Jerusalem, with righteous offerings restored.

chapters.title: Boastful deceit and enduring trust

parts.text: The psalm challenges a mighty person who boasts in mischief, loves evil more than good, and uses words as a destructive razor. God will uproot him from the land of the living, exposing the folly of trusting wealth and wickedness instead of divine strength. The psalmist contrasts that fate with his own hope: like a green olive tree in God’s house, he trusts enduring mercy, gives thanks, and waits upon God’s good name.

chapters.title: God sees humanity’s corruption

parts.text: The fool’s denial of God is accompanied by corruption and evil deeds. God looks from heaven for understanding and for people who seek him, but finds all turned aside. Those who devour his people without calling on God face unexpected terror: God scatters the bones of those encamped against his people and puts the attackers to shame. The psalm ends with longing for Israel’s salvation from Zion and the joy that will accompany the restoration of God’s people.

chapters.title: God upholds the threatened life

parts.text: The psalmist asks God to save by his name and vindicate by his strength. Strangers and violent oppressors seek his life without regarding God. Against this threat, he confesses that God is his helper and the sustainer of his life. He asks that evil return upon his enemies and promises a willing sacrifice and thanksgiving. The closing assurance praises the LORD’s good name for deliverance from trouble.

chapters.title: The pain of betrayal by a companion

parts.text: Fear, anguish, and the prospect of death drive the psalmist to prayer. He wishes for a dove’s wings to escape to the wilderness, away from violence and strife filling the city. The deepest wound is not an open enemy’s hostility but betrayal by a close companion with whom he once shared fellowship in God’s house.

He resolves to call upon God evening, morning, and noon, confident of rescue. The betrayer’s smooth words conceal war and broken covenant. The psalm urges the burdened to cast their load upon the LORD, who sustains the righteous. Bloody and deceitful people face destruction, but the psalmist will continue trusting God.

chapters.title: Trust when afraid

parts.text: Daily oppression and twisted words leave the psalmist surrounded by enemies seeking his life. Whenever he is afraid, he chooses to trust God and praise his word, asking what mortal people can ultimately do. God knows his wanderings and records his tears. Confident that God is for him, he anticipates his enemies’ retreat. He promises thanksgiving and fulfilment of vows, praising the deliverance that allows him to walk before God among the living.

chapters.title: Refuge until danger passes

parts.text: The psalmist shelters beneath God’s wings until calamities pass and cries to the God who acts on his behalf. Enemies surround him like lions, with teeth as weapons and tongues as swords. He asks that God’s glory be exalted above heaven and earth, while the pit his enemies dug becomes their own trap.

His heart becomes steadfast in praise. Calling upon harp and psaltery to awaken, he resolves to give thanks among peoples and nations. God’s mercy reaches the heavens and his faithfulness the clouds. The repeated prayer for divine exaltation frames deliverance as a reason for praise far beyond the immediate crisis.

chapters.title: A call for judgment upon unjust rulers

parts.text: The psalm questions those who should judge uprightly but instead practice wickedness and distribute violence. The wicked are depicted as estranged from birth and poisonous like a serpent that refuses the charmer’s voice. Their refusal to hear correction makes their authority dangerous rather than protective.

The prayer asks God to break their power and make their schemes vanish like flowing water or a failed arrow. Their sudden removal will show that injustice does not hold the final word. The righteous will rejoice at vindication, and observers will recognize both a reward for righteousness and a God who judges the earth.

chapters.title: Deliverance from prowling enemies

parts.text: The psalmist asks protection from violent men who lie in wait although he has not committed the offence they imply. He calls upon the LORD God of hosts to awake and judge. The enemies circle the city like snarling dogs, boasting that no one hears, but God laughs at their threats.

He asks that their downfall become a public lesson, with pride and lying speech exposing them to judgment. Their restless prowling contrasts with his resolve to sing each morning of God’s strength and mercy. God has been his defence and refuge in trouble, so his final response is praise to the source of his protection.

chapters.title: A defeated people seeks renewed victory

parts.text: The people describe rejection, broken defences, and a land shaken by God’s displeasure. They have experienced hard things and ask God to restore them. Nevertheless, he has given a banner to those who fear him, and they appeal for the deliverance of his beloved by his saving right hand.

God’s declaration claims Israel’s territories and neighbouring nations as subject to his authority. The people ask who will lead them into the fortified city and Edom if God no longer goes with their armies. Human help is vain; renewed courage and victory must come through the God who treads down their enemies.

chapters.title: Shelter under God’s wings

parts.text: From a place of overwhelming distress, the psalmist calls to God and asks to be led to a rock higher than himself. God has been a shelter and strong tower, so he longs to remain in his dwelling and beneath his wings. He acknowledges that God has heard his vows and granted the inheritance of those who fear his name. Prayer for the king’s enduring life and preservation leads to a promise of continual praise and fulfilled vows.

chapters.title: Waiting upon God alone

parts.text: The psalmist waits upon God as his rock, salvation, and defence. Enemies try to topple him through lies and outward blessings that conceal inward curses. He calls his own soul back to quiet expectation in God, then urges the people to trust him at all times and pour out their hearts before their refuge.

People of both low and high station are insubstantial when weighed against true security. Oppression, robbery, and increasing wealth must not become objects of confidence. Power belongs to God, and mercy belongs to him also. His judgment renders to each person according to his work.

chapters.title: Longing for God in a dry land

parts.text: The psalmist thirsts for God in a dry land and remembers seeing his power and glory in the sanctuary. Because God’s lovingkindness is better than life, he will praise with lifted hands and find inward satisfaction. Remembering God on his bed and during the night watches brings joy beneath his protecting wings. While enemies seeking his destruction face death and shame, the king and those who honour God will rejoice, and lying mouths will be silenced.

chapters.title: Secret attackers meet God’s answer

parts.text: The psalmist asks protection from conspirators who sharpen their tongues like swords and shoot bitter words like hidden arrows. They encourage one another in secret schemes and assume their plans cannot be discovered. God answers with his own sudden arrow, turning their tongues against them. Their downfall causes witnesses to fear, declare God’s work, and consider his actions carefully. The righteous respond with gladness, trust, and praise in the LORD.

chapters.title: God crowns the year with goodness

parts.text: Praise awaits God in Sion, where vows are fulfilled and prayers heard. He forgives prevailing iniquities and blesses those admitted to his courts. His righteous acts inspire confidence throughout the earth: he establishes mountains, stills the seas, and quiets the tumult of peoples. His wonders cause awe from morning to evening.

God’s care for the earth supplies water, prepares grain, softens the ground, and blesses growth. The year is crowned with goodness, wilderness pastures overflow, hills rejoice, flocks cover the fields, and valleys fill with grain. The fertile landscape itself is portrayed as joining in joyful song.

chapters.title: Praise for deliverance through testing

parts.text: All lands are summoned to praise God’s glorious name and behold his mighty works. The turning of sea into dry land displays his saving power, while his eyes continue watching the nations. The worshippers recall being tested like silver, trapped, burdened, and taken through fire and water before God brought them into abundance.

The speaker promises burnt offerings and the fulfilment of vows made during trouble. He invites all who fear God to hear what God has done for him. He acknowledges that cherished iniquity would obstruct prayer, but rejoices that God has heard and has not withheld either his mercy or his attention.

chapters.title: Blessing that makes God’s way known

parts.text: The people ask God for mercy, blessing, and the shining of his face so that his way and salvation may be known among all nations. They call every people to praise him and rejoice because he judges rightly and governs the nations. The earth’s fruitful yield accompanies the expectation of God’s continued blessing. The desired result reaches beyond Israel: all the ends of the earth are to fear him.

chapters.title: God’s victorious march and care for his people

parts.text: The psalm calls upon God to arise and scatter his enemies while the righteous rejoice. He defends the fatherless and widows, brings the solitary into households, and frees captives. His march through the wilderness, provision of rain, and victories over kings display care for his inheritance. God’s chosen hill is celebrated as his dwelling, and his ascent is accompanied by captives and gifts.

The Lord daily blesses his people and holds deliverance from death. Defeated enemies give way to a procession of singers, musicians, and Israel’s tribes at the sanctuary. The prayer seeks the strengthening of God’s work and the submission of hostile powers. Kingdoms are called to sing to the heavenly ruler who gives strength and power to Israel.

chapters.title: A sufferer’s plea and hope for Zion

parts.text: The speaker cries for rescue as though sinking into deep mire and overwhelming waters. Enemies hate him without cause; zeal for God’s house and fasting have brought ridicule. He admits that God knows his foolishness and asks that others who hope in God not be ashamed through him. His appeal rests on abundant mercy and faithful salvation.

Reproach has broken his heart, and those expected to comfort him instead give gall for food and vinegar for thirst. He asks judgment upon his persecutors, then turns toward praise as the offering God welcomes. The humble are encouraged, because God hears the needy. Heaven and earth are called to rejoice in the promised salvation of Zion and the dwelling of God’s servants there.

chapters.title: An urgent appeal for help

parts.text: The psalmist asks God to hurry to his rescue. Those who seek his life or delight in his hurt should be turned back in shame, while those who seek God and love his salvation should rejoice and continually magnify him. The speaker ends by acknowledging his own poverty and need. God alone is his help and deliverer, and he pleads that the LORD not delay.

chapters.title: Hope from youth into old age

parts.text: The psalmist seeks refuge in God, recalling dependence upon him from birth and throughout youth. God has been a strong habitation, so he asks not to be rejected when age weakens him. Enemies interpret his frailty as abandonment by God and plot against him; he begs for prompt help and their confusion.

He resolves to continue hoping and proclaiming God’s righteousness and salvation beyond his ability to number them. He asks to live long enough to declare God’s strength to another generation. Though he has experienced many troubles, he expects renewed life and comfort. Song, instruments, and continual testimony will celebrate the redemption God provides.

chapters.title: A prayer for a just and peaceful king

parts.text: The prayer asks God to give the king righteousness so he will defend the poor, save the needy, and crush oppression. His rule is pictured as refreshing rain, bringing flourishing righteousness and abundant peace. His dominion reaches widely, and distant kings bring gifts while nations serve him.

The king rescues those who have no helper and values the lives of the poor. The psalm anticipates prayer for him, plentiful grain, and a name through which people are blessed. It concludes by blessing the LORD God of Israel, asking that his glory fill the whole earth, and marking the end of the prayers of David son of Jesse.

chapters.title: Understanding the end of the prosperous wicked

parts.text: The psalmist confesses that envy nearly caused him to stumble. The wicked seemed healthy, wealthy, proud, and free from ordinary troubles, while his own efforts at purity brought affliction. Their arrogance even led them to question God’s knowledge. Yet speaking as though obedience were pointless would betray God’s people. The difficulty begins to clear when he enters God’s sanctuary and considers their end.

He recognizes their prosperity as unstable and himself as foolish for judging by appearances. God has nevertheless held his hand and will guide him. With God as his lasting portion, even failing flesh and heart do not destroy hope. Nearness to God replaces envy with trust and testimony.

chapters.title: An appeal after the sanctuary is destroyed

parts.text: The people ask why God seems to have rejected the flock he redeemed. Enemies have wrecked the sanctuary, set up their signs, burned the holy dwelling, and destroyed meeting places. The loss is intensified by the absence of a prophet or anyone able to say how long the devastation will continue.

They remember God as their ancient king, powerful over the sea, leviathan, springs, rivers, day, night, and the seasons. Because the Maker of these things can act, they ask him to remember the enemy’s reproach and his covenant. The prayer seeks protection for the poor and a defence of God’s own cause against continual hostility.

chapters.title: God brings down the proud

parts.text: The people thank God because his wonderful works show that his name is near. Divine judgment will uphold the earth when it shakes and rebuke those who proudly exalt themselves. Promotion comes neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the south; God is judge, bringing one person down and raising another. The wicked must drink the cup he appoints. The singer promises praise to the God of Jacob and anticipates wicked power cut off while righteous strength is exalted.

chapters.title: The feared God who ends battle

parts.text: God is known in Judah and dwells in Zion, where he breaks the weapons of war. Powerful warriors are plundered and made helpless at his rebuke. None can stand before his anger. When he rises to judgment to save the meek, the earth becomes still. Even human wrath serves his praise, with its remainder restrained. Worshippers are urged to fulfil their vows and bring gifts to the God who humbles princes and terrifies earthly kings.

chapters.title: Remembering God’s unseen path through the sea

parts.text: The psalmist cries to God through a sleepless, troubled night. Remembering former songs only sharpens the question of whether the Lord has rejected his people forever. He asks whether mercy has ended, promises have failed, and divine compassion has been shut away in anger.

He turns deliberately to remembering God’s works and wonders. God’s holiness and redeeming power were displayed when the waters trembled, clouds poured rain, and lightning lit the world. His path passed through the sea, although his footsteps could not be traced. He led his people like a flock by the hands of Moses and Aaron.

chapters.title: Israel’s repeated rebellion and God’s enduring care

parts.text: The people are urged to teach coming generations God’s works and commandments so they will trust and obey rather than repeat ancestral rebellion. The account recalls Egypt’s wonders, passage through the sea, water from rock, manna, and quail. Despite these gifts, Israel tested God and incurred judgment. Their repentance was often shallow, yet he repeatedly showed compassion, remembering their frailty.

The psalm returns to Egypt’s plagues and God’s guidance into the promised land, where the people again turned to idols. Shiloh was forsaken and the nation suffered defeat. God then arose, chose Judah and Mount Zion, and selected David from the sheepfolds. David’s care is pictured as shepherding with integrity and skill, contrasting with the history of faithlessness.

chapters.title: A devastated people asks forgiveness and vindication

parts.text: The nations have invaded God’s inheritance, defiled the temple, and reduced Jerusalem to ruins. Unburied bodies and spilled blood make the people a reproach to their neighbours. They ask how long God’s anger will continue and call for judgment upon the nations that have consumed Jacob and refuse to call on his name.

The prayer seeks mercy instead of remembrance of former iniquities, and asks forgiveness and rescue for God’s name’s sake. The people plead for prisoners and those appointed to death, asking that reproach be answered. As God’s people and flock, they promise lasting thanksgiving and praise through coming generations.

chapters.title: Restore the vine brought out of Egypt

parts.text: The Shepherd of Israel is asked to hear, shine forth, and stir up his strength to save. The people repeat their plea for restoration and the light of God’s face. Instead of the expected blessing, they have been fed tears and made a cause of strife and mockery among neighbours.

Israel is pictured as a vine brought out of Egypt and planted in cleared ground, spreading broadly until its protective walls were broken. Passing strangers and wild creatures now ravage it. The prayer asks God to visit and restore his planting, uphold the man of his right hand, and renew the people so they will call upon him.

chapters.title: A festival call and a warning to listen

parts.text: The people are called to sing, play instruments, and sound the trumpet at the appointed feast. The observance recalls God’s deliverance from Egypt, his removal of burdens, his answer in distress, and the testing at Meribah. Worship is connected with remembered rescue rather than celebration detached from obedience.

God calls Israel to listen, reject foreign gods, and receive his abundant provision. Because the people refused his voice, he gave them over to their own counsels. He laments their disobedience: if they listened, he would subdue their enemies and feed them with the finest wheat and honey from the rock.

chapters.title: God judges unjust authorities

parts.text: God stands in the assembly and confronts those exercising judgment, asking how long they will favour the wicked. They are commanded to defend the poor, fatherless, afflicted, and needy and deliver them from oppression. Their ignorance and darkness unsettle the foundations of the earth. Though addressed as gods and children of the Most High, they will die like men and fall like princes. The concluding appeal asks God himself to judge the earth and possess all nations.

chapters.title: A plea against a united conspiracy

parts.text: The psalmist asks God not to remain silent while enemies conspire to erase Israel’s national identity and name. Neighbouring peoples form an alliance against God’s hidden ones, including Edom, Moab, Ammon, Amalek, the Philistines, Tyre, and Assur. Their opposition is described as a covenant against God himself.

The prayer recalls earlier defeats of Midian and the forces of Sisera and asks for comparable overthrow. The enemies should become like stubble before wind or a forest consumed by fire. Their shame is sought so they will seek the LORD’s name and know that Jehovah alone is Most High over all the earth.

chapters.title: Longing for the courts of the LORD

parts.text: The psalmist longs intensely for the LORD’s dwelling, where even birds find a place near the altars. Those who dwell in God’s house are blessed with continuing praise. Those whose strength is in him pass through a valley of weeping toward renewed strength and their appearance before God in Zion.

Prayer is offered for the LORD’s anointed. One day in God’s courts is preferred to a thousand elsewhere, and even a doorkeeper’s place is better than residence among the wicked. The LORD is sun and shield, giving grace and glory and withholding no good thing from the upright. Trust in him is pronounced blessed.

chapters.title: Restore us again in mercy and peace

parts.text: The people recall God’s favour toward the land, the restoration of Jacob, the forgiveness of sin, and the withdrawal of wrath. They now ask him to restore them again and end his anger. They long to be revived so they can rejoice in him and experience his mercy and salvation.

The speaker listens for God’s promise of peace to his people, warning them not to return to folly. Salvation is near those who fear him. Mercy and truth meet, righteousness and peace embrace, and the land yields its increase. Righteousness goes before God and marks the path for his people.

chapters.title: An undivided heart that fears God’s name

parts.text: Poor and needy, the psalmist asks the Lord to preserve, forgive, and gladden him. God is good and abundant in mercy toward all who call upon him, so the speaker expects an answer in trouble. None among the gods compares with the Lord’s works; all nations he has made will come and glorify him.

The prayer asks instruction in God’s way and an undivided heart to fear his name. Gratitude for deliverance from the lowest hell is joined with a new plea against violent, arrogant enemies. Relying on God’s compassion, patience, and faithfulness, the psalmist asks strength and a sign of favour that will shame his opponents.

chapters.title: Zion and those counted among her people

parts.text: The LORD loves Zion and glorious things are spoken of his city. Rahab, Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Ethiopia appear in a vision of people acknowledged in relation to her. The Most High himself establishes Zion and records those said to have been born there. Singers and instrumentalists join in celebrating the city as the source of their springs. The short psalm presents belonging to God’s city as an honour grounded in his own recognition.

chapters.title: A prayer that ends in darkness

parts.text: The speaker cries day and night to the God of his salvation, yet feels close to the grave and counted among the dead. He describes divine wrath as overwhelming waves and laments being isolated from acquaintances. His eyes fail through affliction, but he continues stretching out his hands to God.

He asks whether the dead will declare God’s lovingkindness and faithfulness, then renews his morning plea. No visible answer resolves the suffering: terror, anger, and loneliness still surround him. The psalm closes with friends and loved ones far away and acquaintances in darkness, preserving an unanswered lament rather than an immediate turn to relief.

chapters.title: David’s covenant amid the humiliation of his throne

parts.text: The psalm praises God’s mercy, faithfulness, incomparable heavenly majesty, and rule over creation. It recalls the covenant with David: God chose and strengthened him, promised victory, and pledged an enduring throne. His descendants’ disobedience would receive chastening, but divine lovingkindness and the sworn covenant would not be abandoned.

The prayer then confronts the king’s present disgrace: his crown is cast down, defences broken, enemies exalted, and days shortened. The psalmist asks how long wrath will continue, reminding God of human mortality and the former promises to David. He pleads that God remember the reproach borne by his anointed, then closes with a blessing upon the LORD forever.

chapters.title: Teach us to number our days

parts.text: The Lord has been his people’s dwelling place through every generation and is God before the mountains existed. Human beings, however, return to dust; their lives pass like a brief watch, a dream, or withering grass. A thousand years are as yesterday to him. Secret sins lie exposed, and human years are consumed beneath his anger.

The prayer asks for wisdom to number those brief days, and for the LORD to return in compassion. The people seek morning satisfaction in mercy, joy corresponding to former affliction, and a sight of God’s work for themselves and their children. They ask his beauty to rest upon them and his favour to establish their labour.

chapters.title: Safety beneath the Almighty’s shadow

parts.text: The one who dwells in the Most High’s shelter trusts the LORD as refuge and fortress. The psalm describes protection from traps, pestilence, night terrors, and open destruction. God’s faithfulness is a shield, and his angels are charged to guard the person who makes him a dwelling place.

God then speaks promises of deliverance to the one who sets love upon him and knows his name. He will answer the person’s call, be present in trouble, rescue and honour him, satisfy him with long life, and show him salvation. Trust and relationship with God frame the assurances throughout the psalm.

chapters.title: The righteous flourish in God’s house

parts.text: The psalm celebrates thanksgiving, morning lovingkindness, evening faithfulness, and music in praise of God’s works. His deeds bring gladness and reveal deep thoughts that the foolish fail to understand. Though the wicked spring up like grass, their flourishing ends in destruction, while the LORD remains exalted forever.

The speaker anticipates renewed strength and the downfall of adversaries. The righteous are compared to flourishing palms and cedars planted in the LORD’s house. Even in old age they remain fruitful and vigorous. Their continuing life testifies that the LORD is upright, a dependable rock without unrighteousness.

chapters.title: The LORD reigns above the mighty waters

parts.text: The LORD is clothed with majesty and strength, and his established rule gives the world stability. His throne is ancient, and he is from everlasting. Floods and mighty waves raise their voices, but the LORD on high is stronger than their roar. The psalm ends by joining this sovereign power to dependable testimony and holiness: his words are sure, and holiness belongs to his house forever.

chapters.title: The judge who hears the oppressed

parts.text: The psalmist calls upon the God of vengeance to judge proud evildoers who crush his people, murder the vulnerable, and claim that the LORD does not see. He rebukes their foolishness: the Maker of ears and eyes surely hears and sees, and the teacher of nations knows human thoughts to be vain.

Those whom God instructs are blessed with eventual rest from adversity. He will not abandon his inheritance; judgment will return to righteousness. The speaker recalls divine help when his foot slipped and comfort amid anxious thoughts. Corrupt rulers who frame injustice by law cannot claim fellowship with God, who will repay their wickedness and remain his people’s defence.

chapters.title: Worship today without hardening the heart

parts.text: The people are invited to sing joyfully and give thanks to the LORD, the great king above all gods. The depths, mountains, sea, and dry land belong to him because he made them. They should therefore bow and kneel before their Maker, acknowledging themselves as the people and sheep of his care.

The invitation becomes a warning to hear God’s voice today and not harden their hearts as their ancestors did in the wilderness. Despite seeing his works, that generation tested him and wandered inwardly. God’s response was an oath in wrath that they would not enter his rest.

chapters.title: Declare his glory among the nations

parts.text: All the earth is called to sing a new song and proclaim the LORD’s salvation day after day. His glory belongs among every people, for the nations’ gods are idols while he made the heavens. Nations should bring offerings, ascribe glory and strength, and worship in the beauty of holiness.

The proclamation that the LORD reigns brings assurance of stable and righteous government. Heaven, earth, sea, fields, and trees are invited to rejoice before him. Their celebration looks toward his coming judgment, when he will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with truth.

chapters.title: Joy before the LORD’s righteous reign

parts.text: The earth and distant islands are called to rejoice because the LORD reigns. Clouds, fire, lightning, and melting hills express the overwhelming force of his presence. Righteousness and judgment support his throne, and the heavens declare his righteousness while all peoples see his glory.

Idol worshippers are shamed, and Zion rejoices in God’s judgments and exaltation above all gods. Those who love the LORD must hate evil. He preserves his faithful people and rescues them from wicked hands. Light and gladness await the upright, who are called to rejoice and give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness.

chapters.title: A new song for revealed salvation

parts.text: The people sing a new song because the LORD has won victory and openly revealed his salvation and righteousness to the nations. Remembering mercy and truth toward Israel, he has made his salvation visible to the ends of the earth. Instruments, trumpets, and joyful voices honour him as king. Seas, rivers, and hills join the celebration, because he comes to judge the world righteously and its peoples with fairness.

chapters.title: The holy king who answers prayer

parts.text: The LORD reigns from between the cherubims, causing the peoples and earth to tremble. Great in Zion and exalted above all nations, he deserves praise for his holy name. His kingly power loves justice and establishes equity in Jacob. Worshippers are called to bow at his footstool because he is holy.

Moses, Aaron, and Samuel are remembered among those who called upon the LORD and received answers. God spoke from the cloud, forgave his people, and also punished their wrongdoing. The psalm repeats the call to exalt and worship him at his holy hill, grounding reverence in the holiness of the LORD himself.

chapters.title: Enter with thanksgiving

parts.text: All lands are invited to serve the LORD gladly and approach him with joyful singing. He is God and Creator; his people belong to him as the sheep of his pasture. They should enter his gates with thanksgiving, his courts with praise, and bless his name. The reason is enduring and simple: the LORD is good, his mercy is everlasting, and his truth continues through every generation.

chapters.title: A resolve to govern with integrity

parts.text: The speaker sings of mercy and judgment and resolves to walk wisely and sincerely within his own house. He refuses to set wickedness before his eyes or welcome corrupt conduct. Secret slander, arrogance, and deceit have no place in his service. Instead, he will seek faithful people who live uprightly. His commitment extends beyond private character to public responsibility: evildoers are to be removed from the LORD’s city rather than protected by its ruler.

chapters.title: A frail life appeals to the everlasting LORD

parts.text: The afflicted speaker asks God to hear quickly as his days vanish, body wastes, and loneliness resembles solitary birds among ruins. Enemies mock, and he feels lifted up only to be cast down. Against his fading life stands the LORD’s enduring throne. God’s compassion will restore Zion, causing nations and kings to fear his name.

The rebuilding and answered prayers are to be recorded for a future people. God looks down to hear prisoners and release those appointed to death, gathering kingdoms to serve him. Though the speaker’s strength fails, the Creator outlasts the changing heavens and earth. His unchanging years secure the future of his servants’ children.

chapters.title: Remember all the LORD’s benefits

parts.text: The psalmist calls his whole being to bless the LORD and remember forgiveness, healing, redemption, mercy, and renewed strength. God acts for the oppressed and made his ways known to Moses. Slow to anger and abundant in mercy, he does not treat his people as their sins deserve. His mercy is as high as heaven, and he removes transgressions as far as east from west.

God’s compassion resembles a father’s care, remembering that humans are dust and flourish only briefly like grass. His mercy, however, endures toward those who fear him and keep his covenant. The psalm calls angels, heavenly hosts, and all God’s works to join in blessing his sovereign name.

chapters.title: The wisdom and generosity of creation

parts.text: The LORD’s majesty is pictured through light, sky, clouds, winds, and fire. He establishes the earth, sets boundaries for waters, supplies springs, and waters mountains. Plants provide food for animals and people; trees and rocks shelter living creatures. Moon and sun mark seasons, night brings beasts to hunt, and daylight sends people to their work.

The sea also teems with creatures, including leviathan. Every living thing depends upon God’s provision and breath; when he withdraws it, they die, and when he sends his spirit, life is created and the earth renewed. The psalmist rejoices in God’s wisdom and asks that wickedness disappear from his world.

chapters.title: Remember the covenant and the journey to the land

parts.text: The people are called to thank God, proclaim his works, and seek his face. He remembers the covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, promising Canaan while they were few and wandering. He protected them among nations. When famine came, Joseph’s sale and imprisonment preceded his rise to authority, preparing the way for preservation.

Israel multiplied in Egypt and then faced hostility. God sent Moses and Aaron, displayed signs and plagues, and brought his people out with wealth and strength. Cloud, fire, quail, manna, and water sustained them in the wilderness. He gave them the lands and labour of other peoples so they would observe his statutes and laws.

chapters.title: Confessing Israel’s repeated rebellion

parts.text: The psalm praises God’s enduring mercy while confessing that the present people have sinned like their ancestors. Israel forgot God’s wonders, rebelled at the sea, craved food, envied Moses and Aaron, and worshiped the calf. God nevertheless saved them for his name’s sake, and Moses stood in the breach against threatened destruction.

Further failures included despising the land, worshiping Baal-peor, provoking Moses at the waters of strife, and adopting Canaanite idolatry, even sacrificing children. Repeated deliverances were followed by rebellion and subjection to enemies. Yet God remembered his covenant and showed compassion. The people ask to be gathered from the nations so they may give thanks and praise together.

chapters.title: Thank the LORD for rescue from distress

parts.text: The redeemed are called to thank the LORD for enduring mercy. Wandering people find a city after crying out in hunger and thirst. Prisoners bound through rebellion are released when they appeal to him. Fools brought near death through sin receive healing by his word. Each account urges thanksgiving for his goodness and wonderful works.

Sailors overwhelmed by a storm likewise cry out, and God stills the waves and leads them to harbor. His rule also turns fertile land barren or makes wilderness productive, humbles princes, and raises poor families. The wise are invited to observe these reversals and understand the LORD’s lovingkindness.

chapters.title: A steadfast heart seeks victory

parts.text: The psalmist declares a steadfast heart and calls for instruments and early praise. He will give thanks among peoples and nations because God’s mercy reaches above the heavens and his truth to the clouds. He asks that God’s exalted glory be displayed throughout the earth.

The plea then seeks rescue for God’s beloved and recalls God’s declaration of authority over Israel’s territories and neighbouring nations. Who will lead the people into Edom if God has rejected their armies? Human help is futile. The closing confidence is that courage and victory come through God, who will tread down their enemies.

chapters.title: A plea against a merciless accuser

parts.text: The psalmist asks God to answer enemies who repay his love with hatred and surround him with lying accusations. A severe series of petitions seeks judgment upon the accuser, the loss of his office, and ruin upon his household. His merciless persecution of the poor and love of cursing are given as the grounds for these requests.

The speaker turns to his own poverty, wounded heart, weakness, and public scorn. He asks the Lord to save him for the sake of his name and good mercy, so enemies recognize God’s hand. Their curses cannot overturn God’s blessing. He promises public praise because God stands beside the poor against those who condemn them.

chapters.title: A king and priest at God’s right hand

parts.text: The LORD invites the speaker’s Lord to sit at his right hand until enemies become his footstool. His authority extends from Zion into the midst of opposition, and his people offer themselves willingly in the day of his power. The LORD swears an unchanging oath appointing him a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek. The psalm then describes victorious judgment against kings and nations, ending with renewed strength and an uplifted head.

chapters.title: The LORD’s works and the beginning of wisdom

parts.text: The psalmist gives wholehearted praise in the assembly, celebrating the LORD’s great and memorable works. His compassion supplies food, remembers the covenant, and gives his people an inheritance. His deeds are true and just, his commands dependable, and his redemption enduring. His name is holy and worthy of reverence. The closing declaration identifies the fear of the LORD as wisdom’s beginning and obedience as the mark of sound understanding, while his praise endures forever.

chapters.title: The steady life of the God-fearing person

parts.text: Those who fear the LORD and delight in his commandments are blessed with an enduring legacy of righteousness. The upright show compassion, generosity, and sound judgment, and light rises for them even in darkness. Trust in the LORD steadies the heart against frightening news and enemies. Their openhanded care for the poor accompanies lasting honour. The wicked watch in frustration, but their desires ultimately fail rather than overturning the righteous person’s security.

chapters.title: The high LORD lifts the lowly

parts.text: The LORD’s servants are called to bless his name continually, from sunrise to sunset. He is exalted above nations and heavens, yet stoops to look upon heaven and earth. His incomparable greatness appears in his care for the lowly: he raises the poor from dust, seats the needy beside princes, and gives the barren woman a joyful household. Praise is the fitting response to majesty expressed through compassion.

chapters.title: Creation trembles at Israel’s deliverer

parts.text: When Israel came out of Egypt, Judah became God’s sanctuary and Israel his dominion. The sea fled, Jordan turned back, and mountains and hills skipped like sheep. The psalm asks these features of creation why they responded so dramatically, then calls the earth to tremble before the Lord, the God of Jacob. He is the one who turns hard rock into pools and flowing water.

chapters.title: Trust the living God rather than lifeless idols

parts.text: The people ask that glory belong to the LORD’s name rather than themselves, because of his mercy and truth. When nations question where their God is, they answer that he reigns in heaven and does as he pleases. By contrast, handmade idols cannot speak, see, hear, walk, or act, and those who trust them become like them.

Israel, Aaron’s house, and all who fear the LORD are urged to trust him as help and shield. He remembers and blesses both small and great, granting increase to their households. The living worshippers resolve to bless him now and forever, rather than joining the silence of those who descend into death.

chapters.title: Thanksgiving after rescue from death

parts.text: The psalmist loves the LORD because he heard his pleas when death and distress surrounded him. God is gracious, righteous, and merciful, preserving the simple and helping the lowly. Delivered from death, tears, and stumbling, the speaker calls his soul back to rest and resolves to walk before God among the living.

He asks how to repay such benefits and answers with thanksgiving, calling upon God’s name, and the public fulfilment of vows. The death of the LORD’s saints is precious in his sight. As a servant whose bonds have been loosed, the psalmist will offer thanksgiving in the courts of God’s house at Jerusalem.

chapters.title: All nations are called to praise

parts.text: All nations and peoples are invited to praise the LORD. The reason reaches beyond any single moment: his merciful kindness toward his people is great, and his truth endures forever. This shortest psalm combines a universal call to worship with the enduring character of the God being praised.

chapters.title: The rejected stone and the day of rejoicing

parts.text: Israel, Aaron’s house, and all who fear the LORD are called to confess his enduring mercy. The speaker recalls distress, surrounding nations, and violent pressure, yet finds help in God’s name. Trust in the LORD is better than confidence in people or princes. God has chastened him but preserved his life so he can declare the LORD’s works.

Entering the gates of righteousness, he gives thanks for salvation. The stone rejected by builders has become the chief cornerstone, a marvelous work of the LORD. The people rejoice in his appointed day, ask for salvation, and bless the one who comes in his name. Thanksgiving and sacrifice close the celebration.

chapters.title: A lifelong prayer to walk in God’s word

parts.text: The psalm opens with the blessedness of those who walk in the LORD’s law. The speaker seeks cleansing through God’s word, hides it in his heart against sin, and asks for opened eyes. Amid reproach and heaviness, he chooses the way of truth and asks God to teach and strengthen him.

He asks for understanding, a heart turned toward God’s testimonies rather than covetousness, and mercy according to God’s word. He will speak of the testimonies before kings without shame. The promises comfort him in affliction; he remembers God’s name in the night and hastens to keep his commandments.

Affliction has taught him to keep God’s statutes, which he values above gold and silver. He pleads for mercy while the proud persecute him and his soul longs for salvation. God’s word is settled in heaven, his faithfulness endures, and the speaker will never forget the precepts that have quickened him.

Meditation on God’s law gives understanding, and his word is a lamp unto the speaker’s feet and a light unto his path. He resolves to keep it despite affliction and snares. He rejects vain thoughts, seeks God’s upholding help against oppressors, and loves the commandments above fine gold.

God’s testimonies are wonderful, and the entrance of his words gives light. The speaker asks for ordered steps, deliverance, and God’s face shining upon him. He weeps because others disregard the law, affirms the righteousness of God’s judgments, and cries for help before dawn, meditating on God’s word before the night watches. God’s testimonies are founded for ever.

He asks God to consider his affliction, plead his cause, and quicken him according to his word. Though princes persecute him without cause, he rejoices in the word and praises God seven times a day. Those who love the law have great peace. He closes as a lost sheep, asking God to seek his servant.

chapters.title: Seeking peace among hostile speakers

parts.text: The speaker recalls that the LORD answered his distress and now asks deliverance from lying lips and a deceitful tongue. Such speech deserves sharp arrows and burning coals. He laments dwelling among people described through Mesech and Kedar, far from the peace he desires. He has lived too long with those who hate peace: even when he speaks peacefully, they are ready for war.

chapters.title: The keeper of Israel never sleeps

parts.text: The psalmist looks toward the hills and confesses that his help comes from the LORD, Maker of heaven and earth. Israel’s keeper neither slumbers nor sleeps, so his care does not lapse. He guards the traveller like protective shade, watching through day and night. The psalm closes with assurance that the LORD will preserve life, guard against evil, and keep every departure and return from now and forever.

chapters.title: Pray for Jerusalem’s peace

parts.text: The speaker rejoices at the invitation to enter the LORD’s house and stands within Jerusalem’s gates. The city gathers Israel’s tribes for thanksgiving and contains the thrones of judgment belonging to David’s house. The people are urged to pray for Jerusalem’s peace and the well-being of those who love her. For the sake of fellow worshippers and the LORD’s house, the speaker commits himself to seeking the city’s good.

chapters.title: Waiting for mercy amid contempt

parts.text: The worshippers lift their eyes to the God enthroned in heaven. Like servants watching a master’s hand or a maid attending her mistress, they wait upon the LORD until he shows mercy. Repeated appeals for compassion arise from the scorn they have endured. Those at ease and the proud have filled their lives with contempt, leaving divine mercy as their hope.

chapters.title: The snare is broken

parts.text: Israel is called to acknowledge what would have happened without the LORD on their side: angry enemies would have swallowed them alive, and overwhelming waters would have swept them away. Instead, the LORD refused to make them prey. Their escape resembles a bird freed when a trap is broken. The psalm ends by locating their help in the name of the LORD, who made heaven and earth.

chapters.title: Secure like Zion’s surrounding mountains

parts.text: Those who trust the LORD are compared to Mount Zion, stable and enduring. As mountains surround Jerusalem, the LORD surrounds his people. Wicked rule will not permanently rest upon the righteous inheritance and draw the upright into wrongdoing. The prayer asks good for those whose hearts are upright, while those who turn to crooked ways share the fate of evildoers. It closes with peace upon Israel.

chapters.title: Restoration and the harvest of joy

parts.text: Zion’s restoration felt like a dream, filling mouths with laughter and prompting even the nations to recognize the LORD’s great deeds. Remembered joy becomes a renewed prayer for restoration, like streams returning to the dry south. The closing image joins present sorrow with future gladness: those who sow in tears will reap in joy, returning with sheaves from the seed carried out with weeping.

chapters.title: The LORD builds the house

parts.text: Builders and watchmen labour in vain unless the LORD establishes the house and guards the city. Anxious toil from early morning to late night cannot replace the rest he gives those he loves. Children are described as his gift and inheritance, like arrows in a warrior’s hand. A household strengthened by them can face opponents at the gate without shame, emphasizing dependence upon God’s provision in both work and family.

chapters.title: Blessing upon the household that fears God

parts.text: Those who fear the LORD and walk in his ways are pronounced blessed. They enjoy the fruit of their labour, and their household is pictured through a fruitful vine and young olive plants: a flourishing wife and children around the table. The prayer extends this domestic blessing toward Zion and Jerusalem, asking long life to see grandchildren and concluding with peace upon Israel.

chapters.title: Afflicted but not overcome

parts.text: Israel looks back on repeated affliction from youth, yet declares that enemies have not prevailed. The suffering is pictured as long furrows plowed across a back, until the righteous LORD cuts the oppressors’ cords. Those who hate Zion are asked to retreat in shame, becoming like rooftop grass that withers before harvest. Their work yields no gathered sheaves and receives none of the customary blessings spoken over fruitful labour.

chapters.title: Waiting for abundant redemption
