parts.text: From the depths, the speaker cries for the Lord’s attentive hearing. If God marked every iniquity, no one could stand, yet forgiveness belongs to him and inspires reverence. The soul waits for the Lord and hopes in his word more eagerly than watchmen await morning. Israel is therefore urged to hope in the LORD, whose mercy and abundant redemption will deliver his people from all their iniquities.

chapters.title: A quieted and humble soul

parts.text: The speaker renounces a proud heart, lofty eyes, and preoccupation with matters beyond his measure. Instead, he has quieted his soul like a weaned child resting with its mother. This inward stillness becomes an invitation to the whole people: Israel should place its hope in the LORD from this time onward and forever.

chapters.title: Remember David and the chosen dwelling

parts.text: The prayer asks the LORD to remember David’s afflictions and his resolve not to rest until a dwelling was found for the mighty God of Jacob. Worshippers approach the ark and invite the LORD to his resting place. They ask that priests be clothed with righteousness, saints rejoice, and God’s anointed not be turned away.

The LORD’s oath promises David a descendant upon his throne, with continued succession linked to his children’s covenant obedience. God chooses Zion as his dwelling, promising provision for the poor, salvation for priests, and joy for the faithful. David’s strength and lamp will flourish while his enemies are clothed with shame.

chapters.title: The beauty of unity

parts.text: The psalm celebrates how good and pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity. This fellowship is compared to precious anointing oil flowing over Aaron’s head and garments, and to refreshing dew descending upon Zion’s mountains. The images convey abundant blessing, and the closing statement locates there the LORD’s appointed gift of life forevermore.

chapters.title: Blessing in the night sanctuary

parts.text: The LORD’s servants who stand in his house by night are called to bless him and lift their hands in the sanctuary. The response invokes blessing from Zion upon the worshipper. The brief exchange joins human praise with divine generosity, identifying the giver of that blessing as the LORD who made heaven and earth.

chapters.title: Praise the living LORD above idols

parts.text: The LORD’s servants are called to praise his goodness and his choice of Jacob as his own treasure. He does whatever he pleases in heaven, earth, sea, and the depths, governing clouds, lightning, rain, and wind. His wonders in Egypt and victories over kings gave Israel an inheritance. His name and remembrance endure, and he will judge and show compassion to his servants.

The nations’ idols are merely silver and gold shaped by people, without breath or effective senses. Their makers and worshippers become like them. Israel, Aaron’s house, Levi’s house, and all who fear the LORD are called to bless the God who dwells in Jerusalem.

chapters.title: His mercy endures forever

parts.text: Repeated thanksgiving celebrates the enduring mercy of the LORD, God of gods and Lord of lords. His goodness appears in creation: heavens, earth, sun, moon, and stars. The same refrain accompanies the exodus, as he strikes Egypt’s firstborn, brings Israel out with a mighty hand, divides the sea, and overthrows Pharaoh’s forces.

His mercy continues through wilderness guidance and victory over great kings, including Sihon and Og, whose lands become Israel’s inheritance. He remembers his people in their low condition, rescues them from enemies, and gives food to all living creatures. The psalm closes by thanking the God of heaven with the same enduring refrain.

chapters.title: Remembering Jerusalem beside Babylon’s rivers

parts.text: The exiles sit beside Babylon’s rivers and weep for Zion, hanging up their harps when captors demand songs. They ask how they can sing the LORD’s song in a foreign land. The speaker binds himself to remember Jerusalem, placing her above his highest joy even under the threat of losing the use of hand and tongue.

The lament asks God to remember Edom’s encouragement of Jerusalem’s destruction. It calls for Babylon to receive what she has done to others and pronounces happiness on those who repay her, including the one who takes and dashes her little ones against the stones.

chapters.title: The exalted God cares for the lowly

parts.text: The psalmist offers wholehearted praise toward God’s holy temple, honouring his lovingkindness, truth, and magnified word. God answered his cry and strengthened him inwardly. Kings of the earth are expected to praise when they hear the LORD’s words. Though exalted, God regards the lowly and knows the proud from afar. The speaker trusts him to revive and defend him amid trouble, complete his purpose, and never abandon the work of his hands.

chapters.title: Known completely by God

parts.text: The LORD knows the psalmist’s movements, thoughts, words, and ways before they are fully expressed. His surrounding presence exceeds understanding and cannot be escaped: heaven, the depths, distant seas, and darkness offer no hiding place. Even darkness is light before him, and his hand reaches everywhere.

God’s intimate knowledge extends to the speaker’s formation in the womb; his members were recorded in God’s book before they were formed. His thoughts are precious and beyond counting. The psalmist declares opposition to those who hate God, then turns the scrutiny upon himself: he asks God to search his heart, expose any wicked way, and lead him in the everlasting way.

chapters.title: Protection from violent schemes

parts.text: The speaker asks rescue from violent people who plan evil, stir up conflict, and speak with serpentlike poison. They hide nets and traps along his path. He confesses the LORD as his God and saving strength, remembering protection in battle and asking that the wicked not achieve the schemes that would exalt them.

He asks that the harm of their own speech return upon the attackers and that judgment overtake violence and slander. Despite the threats, he knows the LORD maintains the cause of the afflicted and the rights of the poor. The righteous will give thanks and the upright will dwell in God’s presence.

chapters.title: Guard my lips and my heart

parts.text: The speaker asks that his prayer rise like incense and his lifted hands be accepted like the evening sacrifice. He seeks a guard over his mouth and protection from inward attraction to evil. The correction of a righteous person is welcomed as kindness rather than rejected, while fellowship in wicked pleasures is refused.

Amid images of judgment and scattered bones, he keeps his eyes upon the Lord and trusts him not to abandon his life. He asks protection from hidden snares and the traps of evildoers. The final request is that the wicked fall into their own nets while he escapes safely.

chapters.title: A lonely cry for refuge

parts.text: The speaker pours out his complaint and trouble before the LORD. Overwhelmed and surrounded by hidden traps, he finds no human protector and no one who cares for his life. He therefore calls God his refuge and portion among the living. Feeling brought very low and pursued by stronger enemies, he asks rescue and release from confinement so he can praise God’s name, anticipating the fellowship of the righteous when God deals generously with him.

chapters.title: Teach me the way I should walk

parts.text: The psalmist appeals to God’s faithfulness and righteousness, asking not to enter judgment because no living person can be justified before him. An enemy has crushed him into darkness, leaving his spirit overwhelmed. Remembering God’s earlier works, he stretches out his hands like thirsty ground awaiting water.

He asks for a quick answer, morning reassurance of lovingkindness, and knowledge of the way he should walk. Taking refuge in God, he wants to be taught to do his will and led by his good spirit into uprightness. He asks renewed life and deliverance, appealing to God’s name, righteousness, and mercy as his servant.

chapters.title: Rescue for the king and peace for the people

parts.text: The speaker blesses the LORD as his strength, trainer for battle, fortress, and deliverer. He marvels that God attends to fleeting human life and asks him to descend in power, scatter enemies, and rescue him from deceitful foreigners. He promises a new song to the God who saves kings and delivers David his servant.

The closing picture describes the desired well-being of the people: strong sons, graceful daughters, full storehouses, multiplying flocks, and freedom from breach, loss, and public outcry. Such a people are called happy, with the deepest ground of that happiness identified as having the LORD for their God.

chapters.title: Every generation praises the gracious king

parts.text: The psalmist promises daily praise to God the king, whose greatness cannot be searched out. One generation tells another of his mighty works, abundant goodness, and righteousness. The LORD is gracious, compassionate, patient, and good to all. His works and saints proclaim the glory of an everlasting kingdom.

God supports the falling, raises the bowed down, and feeds living creatures at the proper time. He is righteous and holy in all his ways, near to those who call truthfully, and attentive to those who fear him. He preserves those who love him and destroys the wicked. The psalm ends by inviting all flesh to bless his holy name forever.

chapters.title: Hope in the LORD rather than princes

parts.text: The psalmist resolves to praise the LORD throughout life and warns against placing final trust in princes or other mortals. Their breath departs, they return to earth, and their plans perish. True happiness belongs to the person whose help is the God of Jacob and whose hope rests in the LORD.

The Creator keeps truth forever, acts for the oppressed, feeds the hungry, frees prisoners, opens blind eyes, and lifts the bowed down. He watches over strangers and supports the fatherless and widow, while frustrating wicked ways. Unlike mortal rulers, the LORD reigns forever, through every generation of Zion.

chapters.title: The restorer of Jerusalem governs creation

parts.text: Praise is fitting because the LORD rebuilds Jerusalem, gathers Israel’s outcasts, and heals broken hearts. He numbers the stars, yet his understanding has no limit. He lifts the meek and casts down the wicked. Clouds, rain, grass, livestock, and young ravens depend upon his care. His pleasure rests not in impressive strength but in those who fear him and hope in his mercy.

Jerusalem is called to praise for secure gates, blessed children, peace, and plentiful food. God’s word governs snow, frost, ice, wind, and flowing waters. He has also declared his statutes and judgments to Jacob, granting Israel a knowledge not given to other nations in the same way.

chapters.title: Let heaven and earth praise their Maker

parts.text: The call to praise begins in the heavens: angels, heavenly hosts, sun, moon, stars, highest heavens, and the waters above are summoned. They exist because the LORD commanded their creation, and their established order displays the enduring force of his decree.

The invitation extends across the earth to seas, weather, mountains, trees, animals, birds, rulers, and people of every age. All are to praise the LORD’s name, exalted above earth and heaven. His glory is joined with care for his people: he raises their strength and honours Israel, the people near to him.

chapters.title: A new song and the honour of judgment

parts.text: Israel is called to rejoice in its Maker and King with a new song, dancing, and instruments. The LORD delights in his people and adorns the meek with salvation. Joyful praise is joined with a two-edged sword in the hands of the saints, who are described as executing the written judgment upon nations and binding rulers. This honour is assigned to his saints, and the psalm begins and ends with praise to the LORD.

chapters.title: Let everything that breathes praise the LORD

parts.text: The final psalm calls for praise in God’s sanctuary and the expanse of his power. His mighty deeds and surpassing greatness deserve celebration with trumpet, strings, harp, timbrel, dance, organs, and ringing cymbals. The invitation expands beyond any one instrument or group: everything that has breath is summoned to praise the LORD. The collection closes with that comprehensive command to worship.
